name: xlgmac_dev_xmit
prose: Writes the TX DMA descriptors for the packet described by ring->pkt_info and hands them to the hardware (dwc-xlgmac-hw.c:702-1008, 'static void xlgmac_dev_xmit(struct xlgmac_channel *channel)'; the packet name xlgmac_tx_post is not the real name and the slice cut the head; returns nothing). The caller has filled pkt_info (desc_count, length, mss, vlan_ctag, tcp lengths, tx_packets, tx_bytes, attributes) and the descriptor data of the ring slots from ring->cur on (skb_dma and skb_dma_len). It decides whether a TSO context descriptor (TSO enabled and the MSS differs from ring->tx.cur_mss) and/or a VLAN context descriptor (VLAN tag differs from the current one) is needed, and computes the interrupt-on-completion flag from the coalesce count and pdata->tx_frames (0 when tx_frames is 0). A context descriptor sets the MSS and/or VLAN tag, marks itself as a context descriptor and updates cur_mss / cur_vlan_ctag; the first packet descriptor then follows it. The first normal descriptor gets the buffer address and length, optional VLAN insertion and timestamp enable, the FIRST bit, and (if it is not the very first slot) the OWN bit; for TSO it sets the TSE, TCP payload length and header length fields, otherwise CRC/pad control, hardware checksum when requested and the frame length. The remaining descriptors get address, length, OWN and checksum setting. The last descriptor gets the LAST bit and, if needed, the IC bit, and records the packet and byte counts for cleanup. After dma_wmb() it sets OWN on the first descriptor, optionally dumps the descriptors, issues smp_wmb(), sets ring->cur past the last descriptor and either starts the transmit (xlgmac_tx_start_xmit) when there is no xmit_more or the queue is stopped, or sets ring->tx.xmit_more. It does no error checking, has no failure return, and does not check that enough descriptors are free.
note: Packet name wrong; real function xlgmac_dev_xmit (dwc-xlgmac-hw.c:702-1008), read in full. Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: am65_cpsw_get_regs
prose: ethtool get_regs handler of the TI AM65 CPSW driver (am65-cpsw-ethtool.c:557-591; slice cut the head; returns nothing). It sets regs->version and treats p as an array of u32 words (reg) with index pos starting at 0. For each entry of am65_cpsw_regdump it writes the module id; for the ALE table entry it computes ale_tbl_len = ale_entries * ALE_ENTRY_WORDS * sizeof(u32) + sizeof(header), stores that value, calls cpsw_ale_dump(common->ale, &reg[pos]) and then advances pos by ale_tbl_len; since pos counts u32 words but ale_tbl_len is a byte count that also includes the header size, pos moves past the end of the dumped ALE words by a large margin (about three quarters of that length more than the words written, plus the header). For every other entry it writes the header length and then, for each register offset from start_ofs to end_ofs in 4-byte steps, an (offset, value) pair read with readl_relaxed from common->ss_base. The buffer must be large enough for all of that; the code itself does no size check, so it is only safe when the ALE entry is the last entry in am65_cpsw_regdump and the buffer is sized by am65_cpsw_get_regs_len (which I did not read).
note: Reviewers: original (buffer-size precondition insufficient: pos advances by ale_tbl_len after writing the header, overrunning), round-2 (pos += ale_tbl_len adds bytes to a u32 index, so the overrun/gap is much larger) and round-15 (gap is ale_tbl_len minus words written, not ale_tbl_len) are all right: 573-578. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head; real function 557-591.

name: icssg_ndo_start_xmit
prose: ndo_start_xmit of the TI ICSSG Ethernet driver (icssg_common.c:861-1033; slice cut the head). It maps the linear part of the skb (a mapping failure logs and goes to drop_free_skb, which frees the skb, counts tx_dropped and returns NETDEV_TX_OK), allocates a first descriptor from the TX pool (on failure it unmaps the buffer, stops the queue and returns NETDEV_TX_BUSY without freeing the skb or counting a drop), initialises it, optionally reserves a TX-timestamp cookie, stores a reference to the skb in emac->tx_ts_skb[cookie] (skb_get) and sets the timestamp request, sets the destination tag, attaches the buffer and records the skb in the descriptor's software data. For each page fragment it allocates a descriptor (failure: free the timestamp skb and first descriptor if any, stop the queue, return NETDEV_TX_BUSY; the skb is not freed) and maps the fragment (a mapping failure frees the new descriptor, releases the timestamp skb through cleanup_tx_ts, frees the descriptors and the skb, counts a drop and returns NETDEV_TX_OK). It then reports the bytes to BQL, sets the packet length and pushes the first descriptor with k3_udma_glue_push_tx_chn; a push failure reports the completion to BQL, frees the descriptors (prueth_xmit_free), frees the skb, counts a drop, and returns ret, which then holds the push error code (the timestamp-skb release in cleanup_tx_ts is not run on this path). On success it increments tx_ts_pending if a timestamp was requested, stops the queue when fewer than MAX_SKB_FRAGS descriptors remain (waking it again if enough became free), and returns NETDEV_TX_OK.
note: Reviewers: original (NETDEV_TX_BUSY path stops queue and returns without freeing the skb or incrementing tx_dropped) right: 1030-1032; round-2 (queue-busy path frees first_desc and the pending tx_ts_skb, not stated) right for the fragment-allocation case: 1023-1028; round-15 (fragment DMA mapping failure does not free/clear the stashed tx_ts_skb) WRONG: 953-957 goes to cleanup_tx_ts which does free it (1005-1009); the path that does not clean it is the push-failure one (983-988 -> drop_free_descs). 2 right, 1 wrong. Slice cut the head.

name: prueth_netdev_init
prose: Creates the net_device and private state for one ICSSG PRUETH port from its device-tree node (icssg_prueth.c:1251-1402, 'static int prueth_netdev_init(struct prueth *prueth, struct device_node *eth_node)'; the packet name prueth_emac_ndev_init is not the real name and the slice cut the head). It returns -EINVAL if the node's port or MAC id is invalid, -ENOMEM if alloc_etherdev_mq fails. After that it creates the command workqueue (-ENOMEM, free_ndev), initialises the work items, requests the port's PRU DRAM region (failure logs and returns -ENOMEM through free_wq), gets the optional tx_ts interrupt (failure returns that error via dev_err_probe), parses the PHY node (-ENODEV if neither a phy-handle nor a fixed link; a fixed link is registered with of_phy_register_fixed_link), reads the phy mode (error returned) and rejects modes other than MII or RGMII with TX delay (-EINVAL); RGMII_ID becomes RGMII_RXID and RGMII_TXID becomes RGMII because the hardware always adds TX delay, and RGMII/RGMII_RXID are rejected with -EINVAL. It takes the MAC address from the device tree (using a random address with a warning if invalid; the of_get_ethdev_address return value itself is not checked), sets MTU limits, ops and features, adds NAPI and the RX hrtimer and stores the emac in prueth->emac[mac]; it returns 0. The failure labels free (release the DRAM region), free_wq (destroy the workqueue) and free_ndev (clear ndev, clear prueth->emac[mac], free_netdev) run in that order; they do not deregister a fixed-link PHY registered earlier or drop the phy_node reference.
note: Packet name wrong and slice cut the head; real function prueth_netdev_init (1251-1402), read in full. Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: tlan_hash_func
prose: Computes the 6-bit TLAN multicast hash of a 6-byte MAC address (tlan.h, 'static inline u32 tlan_hash_func(const u8 *a)'; the packet name hash6 is not the real name). It XORs together, in an 8-bit variable, (a[0]^a[3]), (a[0]^a[3])>>6, (a[1]^a[4])<<2, (a[1]^a[4])>>4, (a[2]^a[5])<<4 and (a[2]^a[5])>>2 (the shifted terms are computed in int and truncated to 8 bits when XORed into the u8) and returns that value masked with 077, so the result is in 0..63. a must point to at least 6 readable bytes. It has no side effects.
note: Contract omitted: the parameter is a pointer. Real name tlan_hash_func (tlan.h:535-544); the old prose described the same computation correctly but under the wrong name. Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: gelic_wl_set_encode
prose: Wireless-extensions handler for setting WEP encoding on a PS3 gelic wireless interface (ps3_gelic_wireless.c:1004-1076; slice cut the head). It returns -EINVAL, before taking any lock or modifying state, if the key index in enc->flags is greater than GELIC_WEP_KEYS. It then takes wl->lock (spin_lock_irqsave) and treats a non-zero index as 1-based (index_specified) or uses the current key. If IW_ENCODE_NOKEY is set it changes only settings: the intended 'only change the current key index' branch tests '!flags && index_specified', but flags includes IW_ENCODE_NOKEY inside this block, so that condition cannot be true and the current key index is never changed there; IW_ENCODE_DISABLED without an index disables both ciphers and clears all enabled keys, with an index clears only that key's enabled bit; OPEN and RESTRICTED select the authentication method. Otherwise (a key is supplied) it returns -EINVAL via done if the key length exceeds IW_ENCODING_TOKEN_MAX, else stores the key and length, marks it enabled and sets both cipher methods to WEP. On every path that does not return -EINVAL it sets GELIC_WL_STAT_CONFIGURED, including when only IW_ENCODE_NOKEY was given and nothing else changed. It unlocks and returns 0 or -EINVAL.
note: Round-15 reviewer (success path with only IW_ENCODE_NOKEY sets CONFIGURED without updating key or settings) right: 1035-1071 (and the dead '!flags' test at 1037). Slice cut the head; real function 1004-1076.

name: velocity_suspend
prose: System-suspend handler of the VIA Velocity driver (via-velocity.c:3125-3158). The device's drvdata is the net_device. If the interface is not running it returns 0 with no other effect. Otherwise it detaches the net_device first (netif_device_detach, before taking the lock), then under vptr->lock (spin_lock_irqsave) saves PCI state. If Wake-on-LAN is enabled it reads the IP address (velocity_get_ip) first, then saves the context, shuts the chip down, programs WOL, enables PCI wake for D3hot and sets the power state to D3hot. Without WOL it saves the context, shuts down, calls pci_disable_device and sets D3hot. It unlocks and returns 0; it has no error return.
note: Reviewers: original (netif_device_detach occurs before spin_lock, not under vptr->lock) right: 3134-3136; round-2 (omits pci_disable_device in the non-WOL path) right: 3151-3152; round-15 (in the WOL path velocity_get_ip runs before save_context/shutdown, not after) right: 3141-3143. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head; real function 3125-3158.

name: wx_host_interface_command_s
prose: Sends a command to the Wangxun management firmware through the software mailbox (wx_hw.c:289-375; slice cut the head). It acquires the SW mailbox semaphore with wx_acquire_sw_sync (WX_MNG_SWFW_SYNC_SW_MB); if that fails it returns the error immediately without touching the mailbox and without releasing anything. Otherwise it writes the command words (length >> 2 dwords, with write-flush reads) into WX_MNG_MBOX, sets the SWRDY bit, and waits up to timeout milliseconds for FWRDY with read_poll_timeout. It then reads the first mailbox word; if the status byte is 0x80 it logs 'Unknown FW command' and sets -EINVAL. Otherwise a poll timeout leaves status as the error from read_poll_timeout (-ETIMEDOUT) and the function skips the reply. If return_data is false it finishes. Otherwise it reads the reply header, returns -EFAULT if the provided length is too small for the reported buffer length, and copies the remaining reply dwords. All paths after the semaphore was acquired go through rel_out, which releases the semaphore, and return status (0, -EINVAL, the poll error or -EFAULT).
note: Reviewers: original (negative errno not always after releasing the mailbox; acquire failure returns without release) right: 298-300; round-2 (poll timeout returns the read_poll_timeout errno, not -EINVAL) right: 316-317, 327-338. 2/2 right. Slice cut the head; real function 289-375.

name: wx_host_interface_command_r
prose: Sends a command through the ring-style software/firmware mailbox (wx_hw.c:398-479; slice cut the head). It first claims the WX_STATE_SWFW_BUSY bit with test_and_set_bit polled by read_poll_timeout for up to timeout milliseconds (it may sleep); if that times out it returns the poll error without changing the sequence index or clearing the bit. Otherwise it stamps the header with wx->swfw_index, writes the command dwords to WX_SW2FW_MBOX, pulses the VLD bit to notify the firmware, and polls for the firmware reply with wx_poll_fw_reply (a timeout logs and goes to rel_out with the poll error). A reply status of 0x80 logs 'Unknown FW command' and gives -EINVAL. Without return_data it finishes; otherwise, if the reply buffer length is non-zero it returns -EFAULT when the caller's length is too small and else reads the reply dwords from WX_FW2SW_MBOX. rel_out advances wx->swfw_index (wrapping at WX_HIC_HDR_INDEX_MAX), clears WX_STATE_SWFW_BUSY and returns the error (0 on success); this is the only path that clears the busy bit, and it runs only after the busy bit was acquired.
note: Reviewers: original (claims it always clears busy and advances the index; lock timeout returns early without either) right: 412-415; round-2 (reply-poll timeout returns the read_poll_timeout errno, not -EINVAL; busy bit need not be clear on entry) right: 434-440. 2/2 right. Slice cut the head; real function 398-479.

name: wx_host_interface_command
prose: Entry point for sending a host-interface command to the Wangxun firmware (wx_hw.c:495-514; slice cut the head). It returns -EINVAL, logging an error and without touching hardware or any lock, if length is 0, is greater than WX_HI_MAX_BLOCK_BYTE_LENGTH, or is not a multiple of 4. Otherwise it dispatches to wx_host_interface_command_r if WX_FLAG_SWFW_RING is set in wx->flags, else to wx_host_interface_command_s, and returns that function's result. Semaphore or busy-bit handling and release happen inside the called function: the acquire failure in _s and the lock timeout in _r return early with nothing to release, and a poll timeout inside either returns the read_poll_timeout error (not -EINVAL).
note: Reviewers: round-1 (claims release on every dispatched path, but early _r timeout and _s acquire failure return without release) right: 412-415, 298-300 (nothing was acquired on those paths); round-2 (timeout paths return the read_poll_timeout errno, not -EINVAL) right: 316-317, 434-440. 2/2 right. Slice cut the head; real function 495-514.

name: wx_configure_rx_ring_vf
prose: Configures and enables one VF receive ring of a Wangxun adapter (wx_vf_lib.c, 'void wx_configure_rx_ring_vf(struct wx *wx, struct wx_ring *ring)' at about lines 228-283; the packet item is only its last part and its name was elided; returns nothing). It reads the current VXRXDCTL value and disables the queue (wx_disable_rx_queue), writes the descriptor base address registers, sets the PCIe relaxed-ordering enable bit, zeroes the head and tail registers and records the tail address, clears the rx_buffer_info array, zeroes the first descriptor's written-back length, and resets next_to_clean, next_to_use and next_to_alloc to 0. It programs the SRRCTL register (wx_configure_srrctl_vf), updates the saved rxdctl value with the buffer length, ENABLE and VLAN bits, RSC enabled with RSCMAX 0, and DESC_MERGE if WX_FLAG_RX_MERGE_ENABLED is set, writes it to VXRXDCTL, and finally enables the queue (wx_enable_rx_queue) and allocates receive buffers for all unused descriptors (wx_alloc_rx_buffers).
note: Item was the tail of wx_configure_rx_ring_vf; fixed under the real name per rule 6 (read 258-300). The old prose said 'queue is enabled with buffers allocated', which matches, but did not mention the preceding disable and relaxed-ordering steps.

name: axienet_probe
prose: Platform-driver probe for the Xilinx AXI Ethernet core (xilinx_axienet_main.c:2810-3182; slice cut the head). It allocates the net_device (-ENOMEM on failure, directly), sets drvdata and basic ops, gets and enables the AXI clock and the optional misc clocks, maps the registers and reads the configuration from the device tree. Two DMA setups exist, selected by whether the DMA engine framework is used: in the direct (non-dmaengine) path it maps the DMA registers, gets the RX/TX interrupts, resets the core, autodetects 64-bit DMA pointers (-EINVAL on a 32-bit kernel), calls dma_set_mask_and_coherent and adds the NAPI contexts; in the dmaengine path it only gets the optional ethernet interrupt, requests the TX channel (and others) and resets the channel, and does not map DMA registers or set the DMA mask there. Later steps set up the default coalescing, the MDIO bus (a failure only warns), the PCS device for SGMII/1000BASE-X (-EINVAL if no pcs/phy handle, -EPROBE_DEFER if the PCS device is not found), phylink (phylink_create) and register_netdev. Failures jump to cleanup_phylink (destroy phylink), cleanup_mdio (put the PCS device, tear down MDIO), cleanup_clk (disable the clocks) and free_netdev, returning the error; early clock-get failures go straight to free_netdev. On success it returns 0.
note: Round-15 reviewer (dmaengine path does not map DMA regs or set the DMA mask) is right: those calls are in the non-dmaengine branch (2985-3040) and the else branch (3041-3070) lacks them. Slice cut the head; real function 2810-3182. I read the head (2810-2885), the DMA branches (2985-3070) and the tail (3100-3182); I did NOT read the register/config parsing between about 2885 and 2985 or 3070-3100 line by line.

name: ixp4xx_hwtstamp_set
prose: Sets the hardware timestamping configuration on an ixp4xx Ethernet port (ixp4xx_eth.c:397-442; slice cut the head). It returns -EINVAL if the device is not running, then calls ixp46x_ptp_find(&port->timesync_regs, &port->phc_index) (which stores the PTP register pointer and clock index into the port) and returns -EOPNOTSUPP if no PTP clock is found. A tx_type other than HWTSTAMP_TX_OFF or HWTSTAMP_TX_ON returns -ERANGE (at that point ixp46x_ptp_find has already updated timesync_regs and phc_index). The rx_filter selects: NONE sets hwts_rx_en to 0 (no write to the channel control register), PTP_V1_L4_SYNC sets slave mode and writes 0 to ch_control, PTP_V1_L4_DELAY_REQ sets master mode and writes MASTER_MODE to ch_control; any other filter returns -ERANGE without changing hwts_rx_en. It then sets hwts_tx_en from tx_type, clears old snapshots by writing the snapshot-locked bits to ch_event, and returns 0.
note: Reviewers: round-1 (success with FILTER_NONE does not program channel control) right: 420-422; round-2 (invalid rx_filter returns -ERANGE without setting hwts_rx_en) right: 431-432; round-15 (invalid tx_type path runs ixp46x_ptp_find first, which may update port->timesync_regs/phc_index) right: 409, 416-417. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head; real function 397-442.

name: smt_set_para
prose: Validates and (when set is non-zero) applies one SMT parameter received in an FDDI PMF frame (skfp/pmf.c:1067-1513, 'static int smt_set_para(struct s_smc *smc, struct smt_para *pa, int index, int local, int set)'; the packet item is the middle of this function). pa points to a parameter header followed by its value of pa->p_len bytes. Using the p_type class (0x1000 SMT, 0x2000 MAC, 0x3000 path, 0x4000 port) it selects the MIB object and returns SMT_RDF_NOPARAM if the MAC, path or port index is out of range. Some parameters are rejected with SMT_RDF_NOPARAM when local is false. It looks up the parameter table entry (a parameter without an entry gives SMT_RDF_NOPARAM if its p_type has a class byte, else SMT_RDF_ILLEGAL), and returns SMT_RDF_ILLEGAL unless the entry's access is read/write or set. It then decodes the value according to the entry's swap string, converting byte order and returning SMT_RDF_LENGTH (len_error) when the value is shorter than the format requires. A large switch on p_type then checks each settable parameter's range (SMT_RDF_RANGE via val_error for an out-of-range value, ILLEGAL for non-settable ones) and, only if set is non-zero, stores the decoded value in the MIB (the IFSET macro); action parameters call smt_action and return SMT_RDF_RANGE if it fails. It returns 0 when the parameter is acceptable.
note: Item was the middle of smt_set_para (447 lines); fixed under the real name per rule 6. I read the head (1067-1165), the end (1470-1513) and the list of return/goto statements; I did NOT read the per-parameter cases of the big switch (about 1165-1470), so those are summarised. Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: smt_add_para
prose: Encodes one SMT parameter into the PMF response buffer being built (skfp/pmf.c:542-1065, 'void smt_add_para(struct s_smc *smc, struct s_pcon *pcon, u_short para, int index, int local)'; the packet item is its body and its name was elided; returns nothing). It does nothing if pcon->pc_err is already set or if the parameter's table entry has access AC_S (an action parameter that carries no value). Otherwise it selects the MIB object by p_type class and index (mac, path, port) and the source pointer, computes the room left in pcon, and writes a parameter header (type and length) followed by the value: it walks the entry's swap string converting each field from the MIB representation (byte, word, long, MAC/ID/string and other formats) into the frame, with special handling for parameters whose value is computed from the MIB. If the value does not fit in the remaining buffer it sets pcon->pc_err = SMT_RDF_TOOLONG; for an index or format mismatch it sets SMT_RDF_LENGTH; on success it fills in p_type and p_len and updates pcon->pc_p (new write pointer) and pcon->pc_len (remaining length).
note: Item was the body of smt_add_para (about 520 lines); fixed under the real name per rule 6. I read only the head (542-575) and the tail (1040-1065) with the error labels; I did NOT read the middle (the per-format encoding and the per-parameter special cases) so this prose is high-level and partial.

name: smt_received_pack
prose: Handles one received FDDI SMT frame (skfp/smt.c:460-804; slice cut the head; returns nothing). It takes ownership of mb and frees it with smt_free_mbuf on every path except one: an ECF request that is turned into a reply and sent with smt_send_frame returns without freeing (the send takes over the mbuf). It drops (frees, no reply) frames whose frame control is not FC_SMT_INFO, FC_SMT_LAN_LOC, FC_SMT_LOC or FC_SMT_NSA, frames addressed to another individual address, NSA frames with the A-indicator set, and frames whose length field exceeds SMT_MAX_ECHO_LEN (ECF) or SMT_MAX_INFO_LEN (other classes), the last without sending a request-denied frame. It increments the SMT copied counter and byte-swaps the parameters. A wrong SMT version (SMT_VID for NIF/SIF/ECF, SMT_VID_2 for the other classes) sends an RDF with SMT_RDF_VERSION and frees; an info length that does not fit the buffer or is not a multiple of 4 (except ECF) sends an RDF with SMT_RDF_LENGTH and frees. It then dispatches by class: NIF announce/request updates the upstream neighbour and replies to requests, NIF replies update the downstream neighbour and the duplicate-address state; SIF config/operation requests are answered; ECF replies are checked against the pending TIDs, ECF requests with bad parameters get an RDF (SMT_RDF_LENGTH) and valid ones are echoed back; RAF/RDF/PMF/SRF frames are counted or passed to their handlers; unknown classes with a REQUEST type get an RDF with SMT_RDF_CLASS. An unexpected type sets 'illegal' and logs that the frame is discarded; then the mbuf is freed.
note: Round-15 reviewer (the first illegal-length check frees without sending an RDF, contradicting the claim that RDF is sent for length errors) is right: 528-532 free without RDF, while the later info-length check at 557-563 does send one. Slice cut the head; real function 460-804, read in full.

name: ser12_check_uart
prose: Identifies the UART type at an I/O base for the BayCom ser12 modem (baycom_ser_hdx.c:423-452). It does port I/O on iobase..iobase+7 (MCR, MSR, RBR, FCR, IIR, SCR). It saves MCR, sets loopback mode (0x10), reads MSR, writes 0x1a to MCR and reads MSR again, keeping the upper nibble (b3), then writes the saved MCR back and writes the MSR value it read after entering loopback (b2, not the original MSR) to the MSR port. If b3 != 0x90 it returns c_uart_unknown. Otherwise it reads RBR twice, enables FIFOs by writing 0x01 to FCR, and selects u from uart_tab[(IIR >> 6) & 3], where index 1 maps to c_uart_unknown, so even after the loopback test passes it can return c_uart_unknown. If u is c_uart_16450 it tests the scratch register with 0x5a and 0xa5 and returns c_uart_8250 if either read-back differs. Otherwise it returns u (c_uart_16450, c_uart_16550 or c_uart_16550A). It leaves FCR set to 0x01 and SCR modified on those paths.
note: Contract removed: the function performs port I/O with side effects and its result depends on hardware, so a pure contract is not meaningful (rule 4). Reviewers: round-1 (the original MSR is not saved/restored; the post-loopback MSR value is written back) right: 432, 436; round-2 (can return c_uart_unknown after loopback passes when IIR selects uart_tab[1]) right: 427-428, 442; round-15 (contract omits side effects) right. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head; real function 423-452.

name: init_baycomserhdx
prose: Module init of the BayCom ser12 half-duplex driver (baycom_ser_hdx.c:640-677; __init). It prints the driver info and loops over i < NR_PORTS creating network devices named bcsh<i>. For each port, if mode[i] is NULL it clears set_hw (and it stays cleared for later ports), and when set_hw is clear it zeroes iobase[i] and irq[i]; it registers the device with hdlcdrv_register using ser12_ops, iobase[i] and irq[i]; if that returns an error it stops the loop (devices registered earlier stay registered). For a device registered with set_hw still set it calls baycom_setmode(bc, mode[i]) and clears set_hw if that fails. It counts the device and stores it in baycom_device[i]. It returns -ENXIO if no device was registered and otherwise 0. It reads the module parameter arrays and writes iobase/irq and baycom_device.
note: Contract removed: the function reads and writes module-level arrays and registers devices (rule 4). Old reviewers mechanical only (right). Slice cut the head; real function 640-677.

name: kiss_unesc
prose: Processes one byte of an incoming KISS (mkiss) stream (mkiss.c:301-341; returns nothing). For END (frame end) it clears AXF_KEEPTEST, then, if AXF_ERROR was not set (test_and_clear_bit clears it either way) and more than 2 bytes were received, it calls ax_bump to deliver the frame; it also clears AXF_ESCAPE, sets rcount to 0 and returns. For ESC it sets AXF_ESCAPE and returns without storing a byte. For ESC_ESC or ESC_END it translates the byte to ESC or END only if AXF_ESCAPE was set (and clears it); otherwise the byte is stored unchanged and the flag stays as it was. Other bytes do not touch AXF_ESCAPE (a pending escape flag therefore remains set until END or the next ESC_ESC/ESC_END). For bytes to be stored it takes ax->buflock (spin_lock_bh); if AXF_ERROR is not set and rcount < buffsize it appends the byte to rbuff, otherwise it counts rx_over_errors and sets AXF_ERROR; it unlocks before returning.
note: Reviewers: original (ESC returns without appending; END calls ax_bump only when no AXF_ERROR and rcount > 2) right: 309-318; round-2 (END path also clears AXF_ERROR via test_and_clear_bit) right: 309; round-15 (prose says AXF_ESCAPE is cleared for any other byte, but ordinary bytes leave it set) right: only the END/ESC_ESC/ESC_END paths clear it. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head; real function 301-341.

name: fpga_download
prose: Loads the FPGA bitstream for a YAM modem through its UART I/O ports (yam.c:429-453). get_mcs(bitrate) returns the bits of a stored configuration for that bitrate (searching the yam_data list), or loads a predefined one (YAM_1200 for 1200, YAM_9600 for any other value) through add_mcs, which can allocate and add a new entry to yam_data; it returns -1 if get_mcs returns NULL. It resets the FPGA (fpga_reset), writes the YAM_FPGA_SIZE bitstream bytes with fpga_write and returns -1 on the first write error (logging 'error in write cycle'). It then writes a final 0xFF byte (the result of that write is ignored), reads the MSR, waits with delay(50) and returns 0 if the DSR bit of the MSR value is set (done signal) and -1 otherwise.

name: netvsc_send
prose: Sends one packet on a Hyper-V netvsc device, possibly batching it in the send buffer (netvsc.c:1236-1360; slice cut the head). It returns -ENODEV, before touching the packet, if the netvsc_device pointer is NULL or the device is being destroyed. It then sets packet->send_buf_index to invalid and cp_partial to false. A control message (skb NULL) or an XDP packet (xdp_tx) is sent directly with netvsc_send_pkt, and its result is returned. For data packets it decides, from the pending multi-send packet on the channel (msd) and the send-section size, whether to append to the current send section, to copy only the RNDIS header (cp_partial), or to take a new send section (counting tx_send_full if none is free and flushing the pending packet); it copies the data into the section, updates the packet's counts, and either keeps the packet pending (when the stack says more data is coming and the queue is not stopped) or marks it to be sent now. It sends the displaced pending packet if there is one (a failure frees its send slot and skb), then the current packet if one is to be sent, and returns that send's result; a failed send also frees the section index it used. The return value is 0 or the error from netvsc_send_pkt (not necessarily -ENODEV).
note: Round-15 reviewer (claims -ENODEV is returned without touching the packet when destroying, but the destroy check is in netvsc_send_pkt after packet fields are reset) is WRONG for this function: 1257-1258 test net_device->destroy before any packet field is written (1261-1262). Slice cut the head; real function 1236-1360.

name: netvsc_device_add
prose: Creates and opens the netvsc device for a Hyper-V VMBus device (netvsc.c:1773-1881; slice cut the head). alloc_net_device failure returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) directly (nothing to free). It clears the TX table, sets the channel read mode, initialises each channel-table entry and registers an xdp_rxq with the page-shared memory model (a failure goes to cleanup2), adds and enables NAPI for channel 0, sets the queue-to-NAPI mapping, opens the channel with vmbus_open (failure goes to cleanup), and connects to the NetVSP (failure goes to close). On success it publishes the device with rcu_assign_pointer(net_device_ctx->nvdev, net_device) and returns it. close clears the nvdev pointer and closes the channel; cleanup removes the queue-NAPI mappings and disables and deletes the NAPI; cleanup2 frees the device with free_netvsc_device; the function returns ERR_PTR(ret) in all those cases. The device is therefore freed on those failures, but not on the first allocation failure (nothing exists yet).
note: Round-15 reviewer (alloc_net_device failure returns before any netvsc_device exists, so it is not freed via free_netvsc_device) is right: 1781-1783. Slice cut the head; real function 1773-1881.

name: netvsc_ndoxdp_xmit
prose: ndo_xdp_xmit of the Hyper-V netvsc driver (netvsc_bpf.c:247-291, 'int netvsc_ndoxdp_xmit(struct net_device *ndev, int n, struct xdp_frame **frames, u32 flags)'; the packet name netvsc_ndo_xdp_xmit is not the real name and the slice shows only its body). The caller must hold the BH RCU read lock. It returns 0 (no frame sent) if the netvsc_device is gone or being destroyed. If a VF netdev exists, is running, has carrier, netpoll is not transmitting, it has an ndo_xdp_xmit and the data path is the VF, it forwards the whole batch and returns that function's result. Otherwise it picks a queue (smp_processor_id() % real_num_tx_queues) and for each of the n frames converts it to an skb with netvsc_ndoxdp_xmit_fm (which can fail with -ENOMEM), computes the hash, records the RX queue and sends it with netvsc_xdp_xmit; it stops at the first frame that fails (the failed frame is not counted or freed here), adds the count of frames sent to the channel's xdp_xmit statistic and returns that count.

name: ca8210_config_extern_clk
prose: Static function ca8210_config_extern_clk(pdata, spi, on) builds a two-byte clkparam array and sends it as a synchronous HWME_SYSCLKOUT set request. If on is true it logs an info message and maps pdata->extclockfreq to clkparam[0]: SIXTEEN_MHZ gives 1, EIGHT_MHZ 2, FOUR_MHZ 3, TWO_MHZ 4, ONE_MHZ 5, and sets clkparam[1] to pdata->extclockgpio; for any other frequency value it logs a critical message and returns -EINVAL before any request is issued. If on is false it logs an info message and sets both bytes to 0. In the remaining cases it returns link_to_linux_err(hwme_set_request_sync(HWME_SYSCLKOUT, 2, clkparam, spi)): a negative result of the request is passed through unchanged, IEEE802154_SUCCESS and IEEE802154_REALIGNMENT map to 0, and other link status codes map to other negative errno values (for example IEEE802154_DENIED to -EACCES, IEEE802154_NO_ACK to -ENETUNREACH). It takes no locks itself and allocates nothing.

name: handle_not_macsec
prose: Static function handle_not_macsec(skb) decides what to do with a frame that carries no MACsec SecTAG. It starts with ret = RX_HANDLER_PASS, takes rcu_read_lock itself, and walks the list of macsec devices (rxd->secys) attached to skb->dev. For a device that is offloaded and whose netdev is running: if the driver ops set rx_uses_md_dst and the skb has no METADATA_MACSEC metadata dst, the device is skipped. If the skb has a macsec metadata dst, it looks up the rx_sc by the SCI in the metadata; if none is found the device is skipped, otherwise it sets skb->dev to that device's netdev, pkt_type PACKET_HOST (then eth_skb_pkt_type), sets ret = RX_HANDLER_ANOTHER and leaves the loop through goto out. Without metadata it compares the destination MAC with the device address: an exact match sets skb->dev and PACKET_HOST and returns RX_HANDLER_ANOTHER; a multicast destination clones the skb with skb_clone(GFP_ATOMIC) (on clone failure it breaks out of the loop), sets the clone's dev, calls eth_skb_pkt_type and __netif_rx on it, and goes on to the next device; if the device has IFF_PROMISC it takes skb for itself as in the exact-match case; otherwise it continues. These offloaded paths do not update InPktsUntagged. For devices that are not offloaded or not running: if validate_frames is MACSEC_VALIDATE_STRICT it increments InPktsNoTag in the per-cpu secy stats and rx_dropped of the secy netdev and continues; otherwise it clones the skb (break out of the loop on clone failure), sets the clone's dev, calls __netif_rx, and increments InPktsUntagged only if __netif_rx returned NET_RX_SUCCESS. At out it calls rcu_read_unlock and returns ret: RX_HANDLER_ANOTHER only when the original skb was redirected to a macsec netdev by one of the three offload cases above, otherwise RX_HANDLER_PASS (including after a failed clone or when every device was skipped), in which case the original skb is left to the caller and only clones were queued.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is handle_not_macsec (macsec.c:1007-1124); the packet name was a truncated excerpt. Reviewer (second) was right that the multicast clone path does not increment InPktsUntagged (macsec.c:1076-1084 has no stats update; only 1111-1117 does); rewritten. Also qualified the earlier claim that the caller must not hold the RCU lock: the function simply calls rcu_read_lock/unlock itself (nesting is legal).

name: ovpn_pktid_recv
prose: ovpn_pktid_recv(pr, pkt_id, pkt_time) is the OpenVPN replay check for one received packet. Return paths: (1) pkt_id == 0 returns -EINVAL immediately, before pr->lock is taken and before any state is touched. Otherwise it takes pr->lock with spin_lock_bh, and every later path leaves through the out label which unlocks and returns ret. (2) If jiffies has reached pr->expire (time_after_eq) it first sets pr->id_floor = pr->id; this happens before the time check, so it can also happen on a path that later fails. (3) If pkt_time differs from pr->time: a larger pkt_time resets base, extent, id and id_floor to 0 and stores pr->time = pkt_time and processing continues; a smaller pkt_time returns -ETIME without touching base, extent, id, history or time (id_floor may already have been refreshed by step 2). (4) If pkt_id == pr->id + 1 it moves base back one slot (mod REPLAY_WINDOW_SIZE), sets that history bit, increments extent while it is below REPLAY_WINDOW_SIZE and sets pr->id = pkt_id. (5) Else if pkt_id > pr->id it advances: with a delta below REPLAY_WINDOW_SIZE it moves base back by delta, sets the bit at the new base, grows extent by delta capped at REPLAY_WINDOW_SIZE and clears the history bits for the skipped ids; with a larger delta it zeroes the whole history, sets base = 0, extent = REPLAY_WINDOW_SIZE and history[0] = 1; then pr->id = pkt_id. (6) Otherwise (pkt_id <= pr->id) it is a backtrack: it first raises pr->max_backtrack if delta = pr->id - pkt_id exceeds it, so max_backtrack can change even when the packet is rejected; it returns -EINVAL if delta >= pr->extent, if pkt_id <= pr->id_floor, or if the history bit for that id is already set; otherwise it sets that bit and falls through, leaving id, base and extent unchanged. (7) On any accepted path (reaching the end) it sets pr->expire = jiffies-at-entry + PKTID_RECV_EXPIRE and returns 0. The expire value is not updated on the -EINVAL and -ETIME paths.
note: Reviewers right: r2 (pkt_id==0 returns before the lock, pktid.c:41-43), r15 (accepted backtrack only sets a history bit and expire, pktid.c:107-112,121) and original (max_backtrack/id_floor change on rejected paths, pktid.c:46-52,98-99). Prose rewritten from the return list. Source is a full function read.

name: pfcp_init
prose: Static __init function pfcp_init takes no arguments and registers PFCP with the kernel. It calls register_pernet_subsys(&pfcp_net_ops); if that returns nonzero it jumps to exit_err, which logs the failure with pr_err (loading PFCP module failed: err N) and returns that error; unregister_pernet_subsys and rtnl_link_register are not called in that case. Otherwise it calls rtnl_link_register(&pfcp_link_ops); if that returns nonzero it jumps to exit_unregister_subsys, which calls unregister_pernet_subsys(&pfcp_net_ops) to undo the first registration, then falls into exit_err, logs with pr_err and returns the rtnl_link_register error. If both calls succeed it returns 0 with both registrations in place. The function is hooked with late_initcall(pfcp_init). The error values are whatever the two register calls return; the function does not translate them.
note: Reviewer r1 was wrong (unregister_pernet_subsys is only reached via exit_unregister_subsys after rtnl_link_register fails, pfcp.c:281-292); the old prose already said so. Reviewers r2/r15 about the contract were right in substance: the function registers global state, so the contract is cleared per HAND_METHOD rule 4. Added the pr_err log the old prose omitted.

name: mv88q2xxx_led_mode
prose: Static function mv88q2xxx_led_mode(index, rules) maps a LED netdev-trigger bitmask to the 88Q2xxx LED function-control value. index is unused. It switches on the exact value of rules, with BIT(n) = 1UL << n and TRIGGER_NETDEV_LINK = bit 0, LINK_1000 = bit 3, TX = bit 9, RX = bit 10: rules == BIT(LINK) (1) returns MDIO_MMD_PCS_MV_LED_FUNC_CTRL_LINK (0x0); rules == BIT(LINK_1000) (8) returns ..._LINK_1000BT1_ON (0x7); rules == BIT(TX) (512) returns ..._TX (0x5); rules == BIT(TX)|BIT(RX) (1536) returns ..._RX_TX (0x4); rules == BIT(LINK)|BIT(TX)|BIT(RX) (1537) returns ..._LINK_RX_TX (0x1); any other value of rules returns -EOPNOTSUPP. It has no side effects.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (rules == 1 ==> result == 0) && (rules == 8 ==> result == 7) && (rules == 512 ==> result == 5) && (rules == 1536 ==> result == 4) && (rules == 1537 ==> result == 1) && (rules != 1 && rules != 8 && rules != 512 && rules != 1536 && rules != 1537 ==> result == -95); */
note: Reviewer r15 was wrong about the bit values: TRIGGER_NETDEV_TX is enum index 9 and RX index 10 (include/linux/leds.h:601-614), so 512/1536/1537 are correct; but the old prose returned 3/4/5/6/7 which does not match the macros at marvell-88q2xxx.c:50-57 (LINK=0x0, LINK_RX_TX=0x1, RX_TX=0x4, TX=0x5, LINK_1000BT1_ON=0x7), so the return values were rewritten. -95 is -EOPNOTSUPP on Linux.

name: m88e3082_vct_cable_test_get_status
prose: Static function m88e3082_vct_cable_test_get_status(phydev, finished) polls the 88E3082 virtual cable test. Return paths in order: it sets *finished = false; (1) phy_read(MII_VCT_TXPINS) negative: returns that value, *finished false; (2) TXPINS has MII_VCT_TXPINS_ENVCT set (test still running): returns 0 with *finished false, without reading RXPINS or changing priv->vct_phase; (3) phy_read(MII_VCT_RXPINS) negative: returns that value, *finished false. After both reads it sets *finished = true and switches on priv->vct_phase. M88E3082_VCT_PHASE1: derives per-pair result codes from the TX and RX registers, reports them through ethnl_cable_test_result for pairs A and B, and for each pair either marks priv->pair with M88E3082_PAIR_A / PAIR_B and sets done_phase = false when its result is OPEN, or reports a fault length with ethnl_cable_test_fault_length when the distance field is below MII_VCT_TXRXPINS_DISTRFLN_MAX. M88E3082_VCT_PHASE2: for each pair whose bit is set in priv->pair, whose result is OPEN and whose distance is below the maximum, reports a fault length; done_phase stays true. (4) Any other priv->vct_phase (including M88E3082_VCT_OFF): returns -EINVAL, and *finished is already true at that point. After the switch: (5) if done_phase is false (PHASE1 with an open pair) it sets *finished = false and returns the result of m88e3082_vct_cable_test_start(phydev), which can be 0 or a negative phy_write error and which moves the phase to PHASE2 on success; (6) otherwise it sets priv->vct_phase = M88E3082_VCT_OFF and returns 0 with *finished true. No locks are taken here.
note: Reviewers right on the old prose: original (OFF phase returns -EINVAL with *finished already true, marvell.c:2754-2755 and 2735), r2 (ENVCT returns 0 early, marvell.c:2724), r15 (phy_read errors are returned as-is, so -EINVAL is not exclusive to the phase check). Prose rewritten from the return list. Source read in full.

name: yt8821_utp_init
prose: Static function yt8821_utp_init(phydev) programs the YT8821 copper (UTP) side with fixed tuning values. It calls phy_select_page(phydev, YT8521_RSSR_UTP_SPACE), which takes the MDIO bus lock and returns the previous page. If that returns a negative value it logs the error and jumps to err_restore_page with ret still 0. Otherwise it runs a fixed sequence of ytphy_modify_ext / ytphy_read_ext / ytphy_write_ext accesses on the extended registers: RPDN control, VGA LPF1 and LPF2 capacitor controls, trace control, alpha IPR, echo control, gain control, TH 20dB (2500), MU coarse and fine FR, then PI control (it reads the register, clears the clock-select bits in it with a modify, and writes the saved value back), VCT cfg6 (FECHO amplitude), TXGE NFR, PLL control, and the DAC IMID (two registers) and IMSB (two registers) controls. After each access except the last it checks for a negative result and, if negative, jumps to err_restore_page with that value in ret. At err_restore_page it returns phy_restore_page(phydev, old_page, ret): if old_page was negative the result is old_page (the select error) and the bus lock is released; otherwise the saved page is written back, a failing page restore is reported only when ret was not already negative, the bus lock is released, and the function returns the first access error, or 0 when every access succeeded (the last IMSB write result is returned through the same call). It writes only PHY registers; the bus lock is held from select until phy_restore_page.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is yt8821_utp_init (motorcomm.c:2535-2719); the packet name is not a defined function. Prose checked against the goto/return list (every check goes to err_restore_page, the last write falls through to it). Notable: when phy_select_page fails ret is 0 at the goto, but phy_restore_page returns oldpage in that case (phy-core.c:801-804), so the error is still returned.

name: vsc85xx_sd6g_config_v2
prose: The slice shows only the tail of the function vsc85xx_sd6g_config_v2(phydev), which configures the VSC85xx SerDes6G macro. The whole function: it writes the standard page to MSCC_EXT_PAGE_ACCESS (result ignored), detunes the LCPLL (pll5g_detune), resets and configures the RCPLL, DES, IB and common registers for SGMII, commits PHY_MCB_S6G_CFG, starts the rcpll_fsm and polls PHY_S6G_PLL_STATUS with usleep_range(500,1000) per pass until bit 12 clears or PROC_CMD_NCOMPLETED_TIMEOUT_MS passes, returning -ETIMEDOUT if bit 12 is still set. It then releases the digital reset, applies a frequency offset, runs the IB calibration (waiting the same way for bit 8 of PHY_S6G_IB_STATUS0 to set, -ETIMEDOUT if not), restores mission-mode settings, disables the offset, and re-tunes the LCPLL. The final part (the shown tail): it resets the RCPLL again, selects the extended GPIO page and reads MSCC_PHY_MAC_CFG_FASTLINK (the read result is not checked for error). If the MAC mode field equals MAC_CFG_QSGMII it selects the QSGMII settings (pll_fsm_ctrl_data 120, qrate 0, if_mode 3, des_bw_ana_val 5), runs vsc8584_cmd with the QSGMII MAC command and, on nonzero, logs and returns that value with the extended GPIO page still selected; on success it writes the standard page back. If the mode is MAC_CFG_SGMII it does the same with the SGMII settings (60, 1, 1, 3). For any other mode it only logs invalid mac_if and continues with the earlier values, leaving the extended GPIO page selected. It then updates and commits the LCPLL and S6G configuration, rewrites the DES, IB, common and misc registers, restarts the rcpll_fsm, polls PHY_S6G_PLL_STATUS bit 12 again (nonzero helper result returned as-is, -ETIMEDOUT on timeout), releases the lane reset and returns the result of the final phy_commit_mcb_s6g. Every checked helper call returns its nonzero result immediately; the result of vsc85xx_csr_read and of the phy_base_write calls is not checked.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is vsc85xx_sd6g_config_v2 (mscc/mscc_serdes.c:307-650, in drivers/net/phy/mscc/); the packet name sd6g_config_tail is not in the file. Whole function read. Old prose was broadly right but said the QSGMII/SGMII paths restore the standard page 'whereas the unrecognized path does not' and omitted the early QSGMII/SGMII vsc8584_cmd error return that leaves the extended page selected; both are stated here. Key path in the packet uses the file basename mscc_serdes.c as given.

name: phy_attach_direct
prose: phy_attach_direct(dev, phydev, flags, interface) attaches a PHY to a net_device (dev may be NULL for a standalone PHY). Steps and returns: if dev is set it reads dev->dev.parent->driver->owner; unless that equals the bus owner it takes a module reference on the MDIO bus owner, and if try_module_get fails it logs and returns -EIO with nothing else changed. It then takes a device reference on phydev->mdio.dev. If the device has no driver it sets d->driver to the generic C45 or generic PHY driver and sets phydev->is_genphy_driven. If try_module_get on the driver owner fails it logs, sets err = -EIO and goes to error_put_device, which drops the device reference and the bus module reference (if taken) and returns -EIO. If the generic driver is in use it calls its probe and then device_bind_driver; on a nonzero error it goes to error_module_put, which puts the driver module, clears is_genphy_driven and d->driver, then falls into error_put_device and returns the error (phy_detach is not called on this path). If phydev->attached_dev is already non-NULL it logs 'PHY already attached' and goes to the error label with err = -EBUSY. Otherwise it sets phy_link_change, and if dev is set sets phydev->attached_dev and dev->phydev, copies sfp_bus when sfp_bus_attached is set, and calls phy_link_topo_add_phy; a failure goes to error. It then creates the sysfs links (result ignored), creates the phy_standalone attribute file when there is no attached_dev (failure only logged), ORs flags into dev_flags, sets interface, state = PHY_READY and interrupts disabled, sets irq to PHY_POLL when PHY_F_NO_IRQ is set or the driver cannot do irqs while the PHY has a valid interrupt, sets port = PORT_MII when generic-driven, turns the carrier off when dev is set, and calls phy_init_hw; a nonzero result goes to error. Then phy_resume (return value ignored) and, when dev is set and its parent differs from the MDIO bus parent, device_link_add (the result is stored in phydev->devlink and is not checked). On success it returns err, which is 0 at that point. At the error label it calls phy_detach(phydev), which does the cleanup of references and links, and returns err. The function takes no lock of its own.
note: Reviewer claims checked: original (any attached_dev is rejected, not only a different netdev, phy_device.c:1673-1677) right; r2 (probe/bind errors go to error_module_put, not phy_detach; -EIO can occur after references are taken) right, phy_device.c:1666-1670,1750-1757; r15 (genphy probe failure does not reset is_genphy_driven and d->driver) wrong, error_module_put sets is_genphy_driven = 0 and d->driver = NULL at 1752-1754 (it only does not touch them on the 'error' path, where phy_detach handles it). Observation: the -EBUSY path goes to phy_detach for a PHY that was attached by someone else; the prose only reports what the code does.

name: swphy_decode_speed
prose: Static function swphy_decode_speed(speed) maps a speed in Mbit/s to an index into the swphy speed table. It switches on speed: 1000 returns SWMII_SPEED_1000 (2), 100 returns SWMII_SPEED_100 (1), 10 returns SWMII_SPEED_10 (0), and any other value returns -EINVAL (-22). It reads no memory, takes no locks and has no side effects.

name: plip_send_packet
prose: Static function plip_send_packet(dev, nl, snd, rcv) is the PLIP transmit state machine, resumed at snd->state. It returns one of OK, TIMEOUT, HS_TIMEOUT or ERROR. If snd->skb is NULL or its data pointer is NULL it logs, sets snd->state = PLIP_PK_DONE, sets snd->skb = NULL and returns ERROR. Otherwise it switches on snd->state with fallthrough between phases. PLIP_PK_TRIGGER: if the parallel port status masked with 0xf8 is not 0x80 it returns HS_TIMEOUT without writing; else it writes 0x08 to the data port and loops up to nl->trigger times, each time udelay(PLIP_DELAY_UNIT) and taking nl->lock with spin_lock_irq: if nl->connection is PLIP_CN_RECEIVE it unlocks, increments dev->stats.collisions and returns OK with snd->state still PLIP_PK_TRIGGER and the skb kept; if the status has bit 0x08 set it unlocks, disables and synchronizes the irq, and then either (connection became PLIP_CN_RECEIVE) re-enables the irq, increments collisions and returns OK, or disables parport interrupts, sets snd->state = PLIP_PK_LENGTH_LSB, snd->nibble = PLIP_NB_BEGIN, nl->timeout_count = 0 and falls through; otherwise it unlocks and, when the counter reaches zero, writes 0x00 to the data port and returns HS_TIMEOUT. PLIP_PK_LENGTH_LSB, LENGTH_MSB, DATA and CHECKSUM: each sends bytes through plip_send and returns TIMEOUT as soon as plip_send returns nonzero, leaving snd->state at the phase being sent (DATA keeps the progress in snd->byte and snd->nibble); after each phase it advances the state, and after the data bytes it computes the checksum. After the checksum is sent it adds snd->skb->len to tx_bytes, frees the skb with dev_kfree_skb, increments tx_packets and sets snd->state = PLIP_PK_DONE. PLIP_PK_DONE (reached by fallthrough or when entered with that state and a non-NULL skb): writes 0x00 to the data port, sets snd->skb = NULL without freeing it (the skb was already freed in the CHECKSUM step when coming through that path), sets nl->connection = PLIP_CN_CLOSING, nl->is_deferred = 1, schedules nl->deferred after 1 jiffy, enables parport interrupts and the irq, and returns OK. A state value matching no case returns OK after the switch. This function does not take nl->lock except inside the trigger loop.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is plip_send_packet (plip.c:756-922). Reviewer r15 right: entering with state PLIP_PK_DONE and a live skb runs the DONE case, which only clears snd->skb and does not free the skb or update tx stats (plip.c:906-918); the old prose did not say so. Source read in full.

name: slhc_compress
prose: slhc_compress(comp, icp, isize, ocp, cpp, compress_cid) tries to Van Jacobson compress one outgoing IP/TCP datagram. Return paths: (1) isize < sizeof(struct iphdr), or IP version != 4, or ihl < 5: returns isize with ocp and *cpp untouched. (2) The packet is not TCP or has any of the fragment bits (offset or MF, mask 0x3fff) set: returns isize, incrementing comp->sls_o_nontcp for non-TCP or comp->sls_o_tcp for a TCP fragment; ocp untouched. (3) isize < ihl*4 + sizeof(struct tcphdr), or th->doff < 5: returns isize untouched. (4) hlen = ihl*4 + doff*4 > isize, or SYN, FIN or RST is set, or ACK is not set: increments comp->sls_o_tcp and returns isize untouched. Otherwise it searches the circular cstate list starting after comp->xmit_oldest for a state with the same saddr, daddr, source and dest ports, counting sls_o_searches per step. (5) Not found: increments sls_o_misses, sets comp->xmit_oldest to the last visited state's cs_this and goes to uncompressed with the oldest state reused. (6) Found: the state is moved to the front of the list (list relinked, or xmit_oldest changed); then it goes to uncompressed if the IP version/ihl/tos, the DF bit, the ttl or the TCP doff differ from the stored header, if the IP or TCP options differ (memcmp), if URG is not set but the urgent pointer changed, if the ack delta or seq delta exceeds 0xffff, if no field changed and the packet does not look like a data packet following a pure ack (tot_len differs and the stored tot_len equals hlen), or if the changes equal SPECIAL_I or SPECIAL_D. (7) Uncompressed path: it copies the first 20 bytes of the IP and TCP headers and any options into the state, sets comp->xmit_current, increments sls_o_uncompressed, copies the whole datagram to ocp, sets *cpp = ocp, writes the connection id into ocp[9], ORs SL_TYPE_UNCOMPRESSED_TCP into ocp[0] and returns isize. (8) Compressed path: it encodes the urgent, window, ack and seq deltas into a 16-byte temporary (using special one-byte encodings SPECIAL_I or SPECIAL_D for echoed or data transfer cases), adds an IP id delta unless it equals 1, sets the push flag, updates the stored headers, then writes to ocp a change byte (with NEW_C and a connection-id byte when compress_cid is 0 or xmit_current differs from this state, otherwise just the change byte), the 2-byte TCP checksum, the deltas, and the payload from icp + hlen; sets *cpp = ocp, increments sls_o_compressed, ORs SL_TYPE_COMPRESSED_TCP into ocp[0], and returns isize - hlen + delta_bytes + 3 (or 4 when the connection id byte is included), which is smaller than isize by hlen minus those header bytes. The function takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is slhc_compress (slhc.c:231-473, a second declaration is at 743 in the CONFIG-off stub region). Reviewer r15 right: the compressed header is 3 bytes (change byte + 2-byte checksum) or 4 with the connection id, not 4 or 5 (slhc.c:430-446). Also the early returns cover isize < 20 (sizeof(struct iphdr)), not 'isize<ihl*4+20' as before. Source read in full.

name: slip_ioctl
prose: Static function slip_ioctl(tty, cmd, arg) is the SLIP line-discipline ioctl handler. It reads sl = tty->disc_data; if sl is NULL or sl->magic != SLIP_MAGIC it returns -EINVAL. Then it switches on cmd. SIOCGIFNAME copies strlen(sl->dev->name)+1 bytes to the user pointer arg with copy_to_user (the length is not checked against the user buffer) and returns -EFAULT on failure, else 0. SIOCGIFENCAP put_user's sl->mode (-EFAULT on failure, else 0). SIOCSIFENCAP does get_user of an int (-EFAULT on failure); if SL_INCLUDE_CSLIP is not defined it returns -EINVAL when the CSLIP or ADAPTIVE bit is set, and if it is defined and both CSLIP and ADAPTIVE are set it clears the ADAPTIVE bit instead of failing; if CONFIG_SLIP_MODE_SLIP6 is not defined it returns -EINVAL when the SLIP6 bit is set; otherwise it stores the value in sl->mode and sets sl->dev->type = ARPHRD_SLIP + sl->mode, without taking sl->lock, and returns 0. SIOCSIFHWADDR returns -EINVAL. Only when CONFIG_SLIP_SMART is defined: SIOCSKEEPALIVE and SIOCSOUTFILL do get_user (-EFAULT on failure), return -EINVAL if the value exceeds 255 (no clamping), then take sl->lock with spin_lock_bh, return -ENODEV (lock released) if sl->tty is NULL, otherwise store the value in sl->keepalive or sl->outfill as a u8 and, when it is nonzero, arm the keepalive_timer or outfill_timer with mod_timer for that many seconds and set SLF_KEEPTEST or SLF_OUTWAIT, or when it is zero delete the timer; the lock is released and 0 is returned. SIOCGKEEPALIVE and SIOCGOUTFILL put_user the stored value (-EFAULT on failure, else 0), without the lock. Any other command, and (when CONFIG_SLIP_SMART is not defined) the keepalive and outfill commands, return tty_mode_ioctl(tty, cmd, arg).
note: Reviewers checked against slip.c:1077-1182: original (sl->mode is updated without the lock) right; r1 and r2 (>255 returns -EINVAL, it is not clamped) right; r15 (keepalive/outfill cases exist only under CONFIG_SLIP_SMART and otherwise fall to tty_mode_ioctl) right. Prose rewritten with those points. Source read in full.

name: sl_siocdevprivate
prose: Static function sl_siocdevprivate(dev, rq, data, cmd) exists only when CONFIG_SLIP_SMART is defined; it is the ndo_siocdevprivate hook that lets ifconfig get or set the keepalive, outfill and lease values. It treats &rq->ifr_ifru as an unsigned long *p. It first returns -ENODEV if netdev_priv(dev) is NULL, then -EOPNOTSUPP if in_compat_syscall() is true; both returns happen before any lock is taken. It then takes sl->lock with spin_lock_bh and returns -ENODEV (lock released) if sl->tty is NULL, for any cmd. Then it switches on cmd. SIOCSKEEPALIVE and SIOCSOUTFILL: if (unsigned)*p > 255 the lock is released and -EINVAL returned (the test casts *p to a 32-bit unsigned, so bits above bit 31 of the unsigned long are ignored); otherwise the value is stored as a u8 in sl->keepalive or sl->outfill and, when nonzero, the matching timer is armed with mod_timer (keepalive also writes keepalive_timer.expires) and SLF_KEEPTEST or SLF_OUTWAIT is set, or when zero the timer is deleted. SIOCGKEEPALIVE, SIOCGOUTFILL and SIOCGLEASE store sl->keepalive, sl->outfill or sl->leased into *p. SIOCSLEASE: if sl->tty != current->signal->tty and sl->pid != current->pid it releases the lock and returns -EPERM; otherwise it sets sl->leased to 1 if *p is nonzero, else 0. Any other cmd matches no case. After the switch it releases sl->lock and returns 0. The data argument is unused.
note: Reviewers checked against slip.c:1188-1272: r2 (NULL and compat returns occur before spin_lock_bh) right; r15 (the check casts to unsigned, so high bits of the unsigned long are dropped) right; original round's complaints were about the contract, which is now empty. Added that unknown cmds still need sl->tty non-NULL and return 0.

name: tbnet_connected_work
prose: Static function tbnet_connected_work(work) is the work handler that brings the Thunderbolt network link up after both logins. Paths: (1) if netif_carrier_ok(net->dev) is already true it returns at once. (2) It reads connected = login_sent && login_received under net->connection_lock; if not connected it returns without changing any state (login_sent is not cleared, no rings or buffers touched). (3) It calls tb_xdomain_alloc_in_hopid(net->xd, net->remote_transmit_path); if the returned HopID differs from net->remote_transmit_path it logs 'failed to allocate Rx HopID', releases the returned HopID with tb_xdomain_release_in_hopid when it is non-negative, calls tbnet_connect_failed (which clears login_sent under connection_lock and leaves login_received set) and returns; at that point the rings have not been started and no buffers have been allocated by this call. (4) Otherwise it starts the Tx ring and the Rx ring with tb_ring_start, then calls tbnet_alloc_rx_buffers(net, TBNET_RING_SIZE); if that returns nonzero it goes to err_stop_rings. (5) tbnet_alloc_tx_buffers: nonzero goes to err_free_rx_buffers. (6) tb_xdomain_enable_paths with the local and remote transmit paths and ring hops: nonzero logs 'failed to enable DMA paths' and goes to err_free_tx_buffers. (7) On success it calls netif_carrier_on and netif_start_queue and returns. Error labels run in sequence: err_free_tx_buffers frees the Tx ring buffers, err_free_rx_buffers frees the Rx ring buffers, err_stop_rings stops the Rx and Tx rings, releases the in HopID net->remote_transmit_path, and calls tbnet_connect_failed. No value is returned (void).
note: Reviewers all right against main.c:640-701: original (the !connected return and the HopID-allocation failure return skip ring stop, buffer free and, for !connected, the login_sent clear), r2 (the call is tb_xdomain_alloc_in_hopid for remote_transmit_path, the log text says Rx HopID), r15 (HopID failure does not stop rings or free buffers). Prose rewritten. Full function read, plus tbnet_connect_failed (632-638).

name: tun_attach
prose: Static function tun_attach(tun, file, skip_filter, napi, napi_frags, publish_tun) attaches the tun_file tfile = file->private_data to tun; it uses rtnl_dereference, so it relies on the caller holding the rtnl lock. Checks in order, each returning a negative errno through the out label: the result of security_tun_dev_attach if negative; -EINVAL if tfile->tun is already set and tfile is not detached; -EBUSY if tun lacks IFF_MULTI_QUEUE and tun->numqueues == 1; -E2BIG if tfile is not detached and tun->numqueues + tun->numdisabled == MAX_TAP_QUEUES. Then err = 0. If skip_filter is false and tun->filter_attached is true it calls sk_attach_filter(&tun->fprog) on the socket under lock_sock; if that succeeds (err == 0) the function goes to out and returns 0 immediately, without setting tfile->queue_index, tfile->tun, tun->tfiles or tun->numqueues; if it fails, err keeps that error and the function continues. For a non-detached tfile it resizes the tx ptr_ring to dev->tx_queue_len; on failure it returns -ENOMEM. It then sets tfile->queue_index = tun->numqueues and clears RCV_SHUTDOWN in sk_shutdown. For a detached tfile it only updates xdp_rxq.queue_index (with a WARN if the xdp_rxq is unregistered); otherwise it registers xdp_rxq_info (an error is returned) and the page-shared memory model (an error unregisters the xdp_rxq and is returned), then sets err = 0. For a detached tfile it calls tun_enable_queue and tun_napi_enable; otherwise sock_hold(&tfile->sk) and tun_napi_init. If tun has an xdp_prog it sets SOCK_XDP on tfile->sk. If publish_tun is true it publishes tfile->tun with rcu_assign_pointer; it then publishes tfile in tun->tfiles[tun->numqueues], increments tun->numqueues, calls tun_set_real_num_queues and returns err. For a detached tfile whose earlier sk_attach_filter call failed, err is not reset, so the function completes the attach and then returns that filter error.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is tun_attach (tun.c:690-783). Reviewer original right (a successful filter attach jumps to out and returns 0 before the queue is set up, tun.c:716-723); r15 right that the -EINVAL path needs tfile->tun already set. Added the detached-with-failed-filter case where err is not cleared (the err = 0 at tun.c:765 is only on the non-detached branch). Source read in full.

name: kaweth_probe
prose: Static function kaweth_probe(intf, id) is the USB probe for Kawasaki LSI adapters. Return paths: (1) if usb_check_bulk_endpoints (endpoints 1 IN, 2 OUT) or usb_check_int_endpoints (endpoint 3 IN) fails it logs and returns -ENODEV. (2) alloc_etherdev failure returns -ENOMEM. After that it sets up kaweth, initialises the lock and wait queue, and calls kaweth_reset (result ignored). (3) If the high byte of bcdDevice is zero, it allocates a firmware page (failure: rv = -ENOMEM, goto err_free_netdev), downloads four firmware blobs and triggers the firmware; whether any step fails (the error is only logged) or all succeed, it then reaches err_fw, which frees the page and the netdev and returns -EIO (the device is expected to re-enumerate). (4) Otherwise it reads the configuration; a negative result, a hw_addr equal to the broadcast address FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF, a failed kaweth_set_urb_size, kaweth_set_sofs_wait or kaweth_set_receive_filter, or a failed allocation of the tx URB, rx URB, irq URB, interrupt coherent buffer or rx coherent buffer, each goes to a cleanup label that frees what was allocated so far (URBs, coherent buffers) and the netdev, and returns rv, which is -EIO at that point (so URB and buffer allocation failures also give -EIO, not -ENOMEM). (5) Otherwise it copies the broadcast address and the configured MAC to the netdev, sets netdev_ops, watchdog timeout, mtu from the configuration segment_size and ethtool_ops, initialises the lowmem work, stores kaweth with usb_set_intfdata and calls register_netdev; if that returns nonzero it goes to err_intfdata, which clears the interface data, frees both coherent buffers and the three URBs and the netdev and returns -EIO. (6) On success it logs and returns 0 with the netdev registered and kaweth stored as the interface data. Apart from the -ENODEV and the two -ENOMEM cases, every failure returns -EIO; raw USB errors from the firmware or configuration helpers are only logged.

Reviewer r15 wrong on both points: the broadcast check is real (kaweth.c:1005-1010, hw_addr == bcast_addr jumps to err_free_netdev) and the firmware and configuration errors are only logged, rv stays -EIO (kaweth.c:906,960-1000). The old prose was right except that it omitted that the firmware-download branch returns -EIO even when every download step succeeds (kaweth.c:975-981 falls into err_fw). Source read in full.
